8:["$","$L13",null,{"data":{"chapterId":23,"verseId":1,"chapterTitle":"Examination of Error","totalVerses":25,"verseData":{"id":"v23_1","number":1,"title":"Desire, Hatred, and Confusion Arise from Thought","sanskrit":{"text":"","transliteration":"","translation":"Desire, hatred and confusion all arise from thought, it is said. They all depend on the pleasant, the unpleasant, and errors."},"philosophy":{"insight":"The ORIGIN of the three poisons (kleśas): desire arises from perceiving things as pleasant, hatred from perceiving as unpleasant, confusion from error/misperception. ALL three depend on CONCEPTUAL THOUGHT (vikalpa) — not on inherent properties of objects.","madhyamaka":"Rāga dveṣa moha vikalpa-saṃbhūta (desire, hatred, confusion arise from thought). Śubha aśubha viparyāsa-āśritāḥ (depend on pleasant, unpleasant, errors). The three poisons are dependently arisen from conceptual evaluation, not inherent.","quantum":"Observer-dependent properties: in QM, measurement outcomes depend on the experimental setup, not on inherent properties of the system. Similarly, \"pleasant/unpleasant\" depend on the cognitive setup, not inherent properties of objects.","bridge":"Both QM and v.1: properties (pleasant/unpleasant or spin-up/spin-down) depend on the observer/framework, not on inherent object-nature. The afflictions are \"measurement outcomes\" of our cognitive apparatus.","accessible":"The same rain is \"pleasant\" to a farmer and \"unpleasant\" to a picnicker. The rain has no inherent pleasantness — it depends on the observer. Desire and aversion arise from OUR evaluation, not from the thing itself.","twoTruths":"Conventionally: afflictions arise and cause suffering. Ultimately: they depend on conceptual evaluation, which depends on subjects — not on inherent object-properties.","commonMisconception":"NOT saying afflictions are unreal or don't matter. They CONVENTIONALLY arise and cause suffering. But their dependence on conceptual thought reveals their emptiness — and thus their transformability."},"quantumResonance":{"concept":"Observer-Dependent Properties","score":60,"strength":"Medium","explanation":"QM: measurement outcomes depend on setup. V.1: afflictions depend on conceptual evaluation. Both: the \"property\" (pleasant/unpleasant or spin value) depends on the observer, not the object.","caveat":"QM measurement is physics. V.1 is about cognitive evaluation. The parallel is about observer-dependence."},"animation":{"visualBridge":"Three poisons (desire=red, hatred=blue, confusion=gray) emerging from a thought-bubble. The thought-bubble evaluates objects as pleasant/unpleasant/confusing. Caption: \"Afflictions arise from thought, not from things.\"","educationalGoal":"Afflictions depend on conceptual evaluation. Change the evaluation, change the affliction."},"deeperDive":[{"q":"What are the three poisons?","a":"Rāga (desire/attachment), dveṣa (hatred/aversion), moha (confusion/ignorance). These are the root afflictions in Buddhism — the fundamental causes of suffering and cyclic existence.","realLifeExample":"Wanting a promotion (desire), resenting a coworker (hatred), not understanding why you're unhappy (confusion). Three poisons in everyday life."},{"q":"How do they arise from thought?","a":"Through CONCEPTUAL EVALUATION: the mind labels objects as pleasant → desire arises. Labels as unpleasant → hatred. Misperceives → confusion. Without the conceptual labeling, the raw experience doesn't generate afflictions.","realLifeExample":"A spider: labeled \"dangerous\" → fear/aversion. Labeled \"fascinating\" → curiosity. The spider hasn't changed — only the label."},{"q":"What is \"error\" (viparyāsa)?","a":"Fundamental cognitive error — perceiving things as permanent, pleasant, self, and pure when they're impermanent, suffering, not-self, and impure. These four viparyāsas are the root of all afflictions.","realLifeExample":"Thinking a new car will make you permanently happy (perceiving impermanent as permanent, suffering as pleasant). Classic viparyāsa."},{"q":"How does observer-dependence illustrate this?","a":"In QM, spin-up/spin-down depends on the measurement axis chosen. Similarly, pleasant/unpleasant depends on the cognitive \"axis\" — your values, expectations, and framework. Change the framework, change the outcome.","realLifeExample":"A rainy day: \"terrible\" if you planned outdoor sports, \"wonderful\" if you're a farmer. Same rain, different cognitive axis."},{"q":"What is the practical significance?","a":"If afflictions depend on conceptual evaluation (not inherent object-properties), they can be transformed by changing the evaluation. This is the basis for cognitive therapy, meditation, and the Buddhist path.","realLifeExample":"Reframing: \"I failed\" → \"I learned.\" Same event, different evaluation → different emotional response. V.1 in practice."},{"q":"How does this set up the chapter?","a":"V.1 establishes the DEPENDENT ORIGIN of afflictions. The rest of Ch.23 will analyze whether this dependence reveals their emptiness — and what emptiness of afflictions means for liberation.","deeper":"V.1 is foundational: by showing afflictions arise from conceptual thought (not inherent properties), it establishes their dependent nature. This is the starting point for the chapter's analysis: if afflictions are dependent, they're empty; if empty, they can be eliminated; if eliminable, liberation is possible. The entire path depends on afflictions being dependently arisen."}],"quiz":{"beginner":{"question":"Where do desire, hatred, and confusion come from?","options":["A) Inherent object-properties","B) Conceptual thought that evaluates things as pleasant, unpleasant, or erroneously. The object doesn't inherently generate the affliction — the mind's labeling does."},"intermediate":{"question":"How does observer-dependence parallel v.1?","options":["A) No parallel","B) QM: outcomes depend on measurement setup.
